runs.t: •  Use me, him, her, us, them

slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive.
Point to the title and read it: "Who's who?" Say: "Tonight we describe people: how they look and what they are like."
Read the three lines under "Today you will". Give one quick example of each: "She's tall. She has curly hair." (looks) • "He's friendly and funny." (personality) • "I work with her." (object pronoun).
Kind words only: tonight we talk about hair, height, glasses, beards, clothes, and personality. Never weight, skin color, or age.
Lesson plan: Topic; At a glance: Objectives; Teacher notes: Kind words only.

slides.title: Who's Who?

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these six things.
I can describe how someone looks.
I can ask What does he look like? and What's he like?
I can say which one: the woman with long hair.
I can use me, him, her, us, them.
I can write about a friend.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: height, hair, a beard, glasses, clothes (She's tall. She has curly hair.). Goal 2: personality (He's friendly and funny.).
Goal 3: What does he look like? (looks) and What's he like? (personality). Goal 4: Which one is your sister? → The woman with long hair.
Goal 5: object pronouns me, him, her, us, them (I work with her. She always helps me.). Goal 6: read a short welcome email and write 3–4 sentences about a friend or family member.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.
Lesson plan: At a glance: Objectives; Progress Check.

Really? Why? What happened? How was it? Where? Who with? What about you?
What did you do last weekend?

shapes.name: pic
shapes.alt: Glasses: a pair of glasses + a woman wearing glasses, label

runs.t: He is a man very tall.
Do you know Ana? Yes, I know.

slides.notes:
Common mistakes (never skip this table). Read a line from Don't say. Ask: "What's the right way?" Learners try first. Then click to show the right form. Each click shows one line, in order 1 to 7.
1: hair has no -s • 2: personality = What's she like? (looks = What does she look like?) • 3: the describing word goes before the noun • 4: adjectives never take -s • 5: add the object (her) • 6: after with, use her • 7: He helps (add -s).
Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.
Lesson plan: Grammar: Common mistakes; Teacher notes: Typical mistakes.

shapes.name: pic
shapes.alt: The bus station crowd, people 1 to 12: twelve numbered people at a bus station, different heights, hair, beards, glasses and shirt colors

runs.t: A: Can you pick up my cousin?
B: What does she look like?

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Pick Them Up · 12 min. Pairs, then groups of 3. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3 (two people share the A cards). 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. 5 or fewer: one group; take turns describing.
Round 1 (7 min): each pair has the crowd picture (people 1–12) and two piles of cards. A takes an A card and doesn't show it. A: "Can you pick up my cousin at the bus station?" B: "What does she look like?" A describes the person (height, hair, glasses or a beard, the shirt color). B points and says the number. A: "Yes, that's her!" or "No, she has glasses." Then B asks one follow-up: "What's she like?" A invents an answer. Switch: B takes a B card. (Each click shows the next step.)
Model with one learner (1 min): card A1 (person 7) and the model dialogue: "She's tall, and she has long, straight hair and glasses. She's wearing a blue shirt." → "Is that her? Number 7?" → "Yes, that's her!" → "What's she like?" → "She's really friendly, but she's a little shy at first."
Answers (the number B should point to): A1 Lisa = 7 • A2 Pedro = 8 • A3 Ana = 9 • A4 Tom = 6 • B1 Julia = 1 • B2 Mr. Park = 2 • B3 Rosa = 11 • B4 Leo = 10. The personality answers are invented.
Round 2 (4 min): groups of 3. Each learner describes a person they admire, personality only, with one reason (My aunt is very patient, because she never gets angry.). The others ask one follow-up question each.
Writing: after round 1, learners write 2 of the people they found in the table on the Talk Time page. Baseline snapshot: call about 5 learners (the ones you didn't talk to in Week 1) for 2 minutes each.
If behind: round 1 only.
Lesson plan: Step 5; Talk Time pages; Answer key.

Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip about a friend or family member: one about how the person looks and one about what the person is like, with because or so (My brother is funny, so everyone likes him.). Collect at the door.

slides.title: Before You Go

runs.t: I can describe how someone looks.
I can ask What does he look like? What's he like?
I can use me, him, her, us, them.
A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.
a. a tall man with a beard
b. a short man with glasses
a. She's shy.     b. She's patient.
a. the woman with curly hair
b. the woman with straight hair

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "My brother is tall, and he has a beard." (a) • 2 "My neighbor never gets angry. She's very patient." (b) • 3 "Which one is your sister? The woman with curly hair." (a) • 4 "What's your coworker like? He's funny and friendly." (b)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 look like, 2 him, 3 them, 4 us. C: answers will vary (for example She's short, and she has long hair. / She's very friendly.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help with look like / be like (A, B1, C) and with object pronouns (B2–B4).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 3). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 3 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
Lesson plan: Progress Check step; Progress Check page; Answer key.
